passage:
Beatriz woke in her Lisbon flat to forty notifications. A joke she'd written three years ago about a football club had been screenshotted without its context and shared by an account with a million followers. Strangers were calling her names. One wrote that she should be fired. Her hands went cold and her stomach turned.

She typed a furious reply, looked at it, and deleted it.

Instead she muted the thread, took screenshots of the worst messages, including a threat, and knocked on her flatmate Lindiwe's door. "Can you sit with me? I need to report some things."

Lindiwe made tea while Beatriz reported the threat. Then Lindiwe took the phone, put it on the far side of the room, and said, "Sleep. It will still be there in the morning."

qa.q: How many notifications did Beatriz wake to?
What was Beatriz feeling when she woke, and how did her body show it?
qa.a: She felt sick and exposed: her hands went cold and her stomach turned.

qa.q: Which steps helped Beatriz, and why?
qa.a: She did not reply in heat, muted the thread, saved screenshots, reported the threat and asked a close friend to sit with her, which kept her from spiralling alone. 🤍

qa.q: How might Lindiwe see Beatriz's situation?
qa.a: Lindiwe sees a friend who needs company and rest more than a quick fix, and moves the phone away so Beatriz can sleep.

grounding: An old post goes viral for the wrong reasons and Beatriz, abused by strangers, does not reply in heat, saves evidence, reports the threat and tells someone close.

passage:
It was a joke I posted at nineteen, about how my cousin's wedding band played the same song eleven times. Three years later someone cropped out the context and it spread as if I had mocked the whole community. By Saturday night I had four hundred messages. Some called me names I won't repeat. One said they knew my college.

I'm Sonali, and I'll admit the first night I didn't sleep. I kept refreshing, my stomach tight, typing angry replies and deleting them.

On Sunday Ayesha came over with chai. She helped me mute the words, screenshot the threat, and report it to the platform and the college grievance cell before lunch. My hands stopped shaking around evening. I haven't replied to anyone. That was the hardest and best choice.

qa.q: How many messages had Sonali received by Saturday night?
qa.a: Sonali had four hundred messages by Saturday night.

qa.q: How did Sonali feel on the first night, and what shows it?
qa.a: Sonali felt sick with fear and exposed; not sleeping, a tight stomach and typing then deleting angry replies show the panic.

qa.q: Which steps helped Sonali on Sunday, and why?
qa.a: Muting the words, saving the threat as a screenshot, and reporting it to the platform and grievance cell protected Sonali without feeding the mob.

qa.q: How does Ayesha likely see Sonali's situation?
qa.a: Ayesha sees Sonali being attacked by strangers and needing practical help and company, not a lecture about an old joke.

grounding: The reflection shows a young person abused by an online crowd, who stops refreshing, saves evidence, reports the threat and leans on someone close.

passage:
Hostel counsellor's note, Wednesday.

Lalit came to my office at 11 pm, sent by his roommate Kunal, who had noticed he had not eaten since morning. A short clip of Lalit arguing with a shopkeeper last year had resurfaced, edited to look like he was shouting at an old man for no reason. Strangers were posting his hostel name.

He held his phone with both hands and kept refreshing. He said, "I feel naked. Everyone can see me."

We put the phone face down first. Then, together, we turned off comments, muted his name, and saved screenshots of two messages that mentioned the hostel address. I called the warden that night, and security was told to watch the gate. Lalit phoned his elder sister before sleeping.

Follow-up tomorrow with the college grievance cell. - Maria Fernandes, counsellor

qa.q: What did strangers post about Lalit?
qa.a: Strangers were posting his hostel name.

qa.q: What was Lalit feeling when he said "I feel naked"?
qa.a: Lalit felt exposed and frightened, as if everyone was watching him, which is why he kept refreshing with both hands on the phone.

qa.q: Why was calling the warden that same night important?
qa.a: Two messages mentioned the hostel address, so telling the warden and security the same night made Lalit safer instead of leaving the threat until morning.

qa.q: How might Kunal have felt seeing Lalit skip meals all day?
qa.a: Kunal was probably worried and unsure how to help, which is why he sent Lalit to the counsellor.

grounding: The counsellor's note shows a student abused by an online crowd being helped to stop refreshing, save evidence, report threats and contact family.
